checks: Occupancy is the intersection of C with the affine graph z↦(z,y(z)+ℓ(z)ξ), hence a compact interval when nonempty. The fixed integer p_- lies between k_0 and k_1. On [k,k+1] the shifted weight is bounded by ℓ(k)^d; the uncharged initial partial cell has length at most one and weight at most (ℓ(p_-)−b)_+^d.

In the lift t=ℓ≥b, the coordinate bound 1−b/ℓ is nonnegative and concave. Ambient dimension is 2d+1, and (x−y(z),ℓ(z),v) is an invertible affine coordinate system since b>0. At fixed z, the x Jacobian ℓ^d times the extra cube volume gives exactly (ℓ−b)^d.

If max ℓ≤b the weight vanishes. Otherwise nested closed neighborhoods preserving ℓ>0 have full-dimensional lifts when needed, and the weighted occupancy integrals decrease pointwise by bounded convergence. The increasing limit of their extended convex inverse roots retains convexity.

Reflection preserves the integer lattice and real interval measure. The positive-part operation is applied with the sharpened cell constant from the historical source audit. It supplies no lower bound on the mass retained.
